identificationModule.briefTitle: A Study of [225Ac]Ac-AKY-2519 in Patients With B7-H3 Expressing Solid Tumors
identificationModule.officialTitle: BActinium-2: A Phase 1b, 2 Part, Multicenter, Open Label Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of Intravenous Administration of a B7-H3 Radiopharmaceutical ([225Ac]Ac AKY 2519) in Participants With B7-H3 Imaging Positive Solid Tumors

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This is a Phase 1b, 2-part, multi-center, open-label study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, dosimetry, and pharmacokinetics (PK) of \[64Cu\]Cu-AKY-2519 and/or \[225Ac\]Ac-AKY-2519, as well as the preliminary anti-tumor activity of \[225Ac\]Ac-AKY-2519 in participants with B7-H3 imaging positive solid tumors.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription:
This Phase 1b study consists of two parts.

Part 1 is the dose escalation portion and will investigate ascending doses of \[225Ac\]Ac-AKY-2519 in patients with locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors, including non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), extensive stage-small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), head and necks squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), and colorectal cancer (CRC). Part 1 will also incorporate a backfill strategy to evaluate two dose levels further.

Part 2 is the dose expansion portion and aims to assess the efficacy of \[225Ac\]Ac-AKY-2519 in two separate cohorts by indication:

* Cohort A: NSCLC
* Cohort B: Other solid tumors

primaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1: Occurrence of adverse events by severity and occurrence of serious adverse events (SAEs) in participants who received [225Ac]Ac-AKY-2519
primaryOutcomes.description: An AE is defined as any untoward medical occurrence in a participant administered study drug, which does not necessarily have to have a causal relationship with the study drug. The number of patients experiencing an AE and the number of patients experiencing an SAE will be reported.
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 30 days following last administration of [225Ac]Ac-AKY-2519

primaryOutcomes.measure: Part 1: Occurrence of dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) in participants
primaryOutcomes.description: Dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) is defined as any predefined AE occurring during the DLT observation period, except those that are clearly and incontrovertibly due to extraneous circumstances. The number of patients who experience a DLT will be reported separately for each cohort and by dose level within each cohort
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From first administration of [225Ac]Ac-AKY-2519 to the end of Cycle 1 (each cycle is 28 days)

primaryOutcomes.description: Part 2: Objective Response Rate (ORR) • Objective response rate is defined as the percentage of patients who achieved a best overall response of confirmed Complete Response (CR) or Partial Response (PR), as determined by the investigator based on RECIST v1.1. Up to 30 days following last administration of \[225Ac\]Ac-AKY-2519
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 30 days following last administration of [225Ac]Ac-AKY-2519

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥ 18 years
* Histologic or cytologic confirmation of locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC, ES-SCLC, HNSCC, ESCC, CRC or prostatic adenocarcinoma
* Radiologic confirmation on CT of at least one measurable tumor lesion per RECIST v1.1
* ECOG Performance Status of 0 or 1
* Adequate end-organ function
* Ability to give informed consent and comply with study requirements
* Patients with CNS metastases are eligible if they have received therapy and are neurologically stable, asymptomatic and not receiving corticosteroids

Exclusion Criteria:

* Prior treatment with a B7-H3 targeted therapy
* Prior treatment with a targeted radiotherapy
* Received an investigational agent within the previous 28 days
* Prior treatment with a cytotoxic chemotherapy, targeted therapy, biologic agent, immunotherapy or external-beam radiotherapy within the previous 28 days
* Impaired cardiac function or clinically significant cardiac disease
* Concurrent serious medical condition that would impair study participation or impact the assessment of treatment related toxicity
